newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa signs extradition for Australia's Bell.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa signs extradition for Australia's Bell.

text.p: South African authorities signed an extradition order on Monday for suspected Australian paedophile Philip Bell, clearing the way for him to be deported to stand trial back home.
"He will be handed to the Australian authorities as soon as possible," Justice Minister Dullah Omar said in a statement.

Bell, who faces 215 sex offences relating to boys aged 10 to 18 in Australia, has been in South African police custody in the surfing mecca of Jeffrey's Bay awaiting deportation since he was arrested in January.

Australian High Commission spokesman Matt Anderson said the commission now had to receive the order papers which would then be delivered to two New South Wales policemen due to escort Bell to Australia.
Bell would then be transported out of South Africa on the soonest convenient flight.
Anderson said it had not yet been decided exactly when Bell would leave South Africa. "It is obviously in our interest to get him out sooner rather than later," Anderson said.

Bell, said to be a millionaire, recently waived a legal battle to prevent his extradition in exchange for South African authorities declining to prosecute him over allegations he may have sexually molested a 13-year-old boy during his stay in the country.
Bell, 62, was arrested in Jeffrey's Bay where he ran a surfing school for youngsters, after a 10-month worldwide police hunt.
